availableCommands.name: built-in-browser
availableCommands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses the built-in browser, the browser pane inside the Claude desktop app (also called the in-app browser, the browser pane, Claude's browser, or "your own browser"), whose tools are named mcp__Claude_Browser__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser tool instead. It covers the pane's persistent sign-ins, tabs and preview_start, reading pages as text, site approvals, what the pane cannot open, and what to do when it cannot be reached. It is not for Claude in Chrome (mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.

availableCommands.name: computer-use
availableCommands.description: Read this skill before the first step of any request to do something in an app on the person's own computer (Notes, Finder, System Settings, any desktop app), to look at their screen, or for "computer use". Computer use (desktop control) lets Claude take screenshots of the person's desktop and control it with clicks, typing and scrolling through the Claude desktop app; its tools are named mcp__computer-use__* when the session runs in the desktop app and mcp__remote-devices__computer_* when a cloud session is linked to the person's computer; before computer use is turned on for a conversation there may be no such tools, only an enable__mcp__remote-devices__computer tool, which turns it on. It covers turning it on, picking the right tool, the access flow, and the safety rules for tiered apps, links and financial actions. It is not for websites, which go through Claude in Chrome or the built-in browser and their own skills.

availableCommands.name: chrome-browser
availableCommands.description: Read this skill before the first step that uses Claude in Chrome, the browser extension whose tools are named mcp__claude-in-chrome__* (also called Chrome, the browser extension, or the external browser) and which acts in the person's real Chrome with their own sign-ins; before those tools are turned on there may be a single enable__mcp__claude-in-chrome tool instead. It covers loading the tools in one ToolSearch call, checking the person's open tabs and working in a new tab, site permissions, GIF recordings, console logs, dialogs to avoid, and when to stop and ask. It is not for the built-in browser (mcp__Claude_Browser__* or mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__* tools), which has its own skill, and it does not decide which browser to use.

availableCommands.name: user:deep-research
availableCommands.description: Use this skill when the user's prompt requires (1) researching a topic across multiple sources, comparing options or alternatives, analyzing trends or history, understanding markets or industries, or reviewing literature or studies and (2) synthesizing that research into a comprehensive, narrative report. If you're planning to search the web or internal knowledge bases, consider using this skill. This skill coordinates research subagents, so use it only when you have a tool for spawning subagents (the Agent or Task tool); otherwise, research the question directly.

availableCommands.name: browser-automation
availableCommands.description: Load a web page in a headless browser and check what actually rendered — console errors, failed network requests, the DOM, and a screenshot you look at. Use it to verify your own web work before you say it is done, instead of asking the user to look at the screen. Triggers on: check the page, does it render, verify the UI, QA the app, is it broken, console errors, did my change work.

availableCommands.name: cf-mui-v9-convert
availableCommands.description: Converts one repo (host, remote or standalone app) from MUI v4 to MUI v9 for LH-54391 the agreed way — build-time alias on the host only, direct import rewrite to @creative-force/cf-mui subpaths (Babel AST codemod) on every other repo, setupMui + CFMuiProvider, package.json/lockfile, repo-specific fixes — then verifies it for the developer: build, related tests, one-copy check, a QA audit of the converted branch (cf-mui-v9-qa-audit --working-tree), and a browser comparison of computed styles (v4 on the Dev env vs the local v9 branch) on the rows that audit marked High. After the PR is merged and deployed, it re-checks the Dev env, finishes the QA scope and moves the Jira ticket to Testing (step 8). Use when a developer asks to migrate/convert a repo to MUI v9, to wire cf-mui into an app, says "/cf-mui-v9-convert <repo>", or says a converted repo is merged and deployed to the Dev env. For developers during development only; QA's manual test cases come from cf-mui-v9-qa-audit, which this flow runs after convers

availableCommands.name: cf-mui-v9-qa-audit
availableCommands.description: Risk-based QA audit for the MUI v4 → v9 migration (LH-54391) of one repo (host, remote or standalone app). Scans every MUI call site, SCSS selector and JSS theme read, splits the repo into small modules (grouped into area folders for large repos), plans agent batches with a script, fans out writer sub-agents in waves to confirm risk, trace each risky site to a screen and the user action that opens it and write the manual test cases per module into the epic's qa/ folder, then verifies the High rows adversarially. Runs on the repo's conversion branch after conversion (cf-mui-v9-convert step 5b). Use when someone asks to audit a repo for the MUI v9 migration, to write or refresh the MUI v9 QA test cases, or says "/cf-mui-v9-qa-audit <repo>". Read-only on the repo; writes only into web-project-docs. Does not convert code (that is cf-mui-v9-convert) and never drives a browser.

availableCommands.name: cf-vuln
availableCommands.description: Scan, triage, fix and report the monthly security-report vulnerabilities for the Creative Force npm web repos (lighthousewebapp, kanbanwebapp, copywritingwebapp, workflowswebapp, vendorportal, commonweblib). Reproduces the scanner locally (npm audit --production), compares the report with master, sorts every finding into fix-now / blocked-by-CF-lib / no-patch / not-shipped / dev-only / blind-spot, and after the dev approves the plan applies the verified npm 6 recipes and opens PRs. Use when the user mentions a "Vulnerabilities - MM-YYYY" Jira ticket, the WEB-1/WEB-2 vulnerability report xlsx, "vuls", "vulns", npm audit, a CVE in a web repo, or asks what is left / what cannot be fixed.

Any engine: if detect finds no preset, write the three-field manifest (launch, log, sourceRoots) and run.

availableCommands.name: chorus-calls
availableCommands.description: Chorus call recordings for BOTH Creative Force and Dreem (one Chorus workspace; query the cleaned views in BigQuery tina-455608.chorus_derived first, raw tables in chorus_us as fallback). Use every time Kristian asks about calls, Chorus, sales calls, Dreem calls, call transcripts, 'what was said on the call with X', 'did pricing / competitors / next steps come up', talk ratios, call volume per rep, or which calls sit behind a deal or stage move. Also trigger for requests like "explain this to my PM", "what does this function do in plain English", "roast my code", "review this", "any issues here?", or "translate this for finance/support/product". Always trigger when code is pasted alongside any question about its behavior, quality, or business meaning.
